title: Authorship responsibilities of scientists who use AI research agents
key_facts: A paper in Frontiers in Genetics (vol. 17, 2026) by authors at the US National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences, Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine and Sigma Xi.
It defines 'AI research agents' (AIRAs) as tools able to perform research independently.
It argues AIRAs do not qualify for authorship because they cannot be held morally responsible.
Human scientists who use them have three duties: oversee and manage the agent, disclose its contribution accurately, and answer for the research to the community and public.
Future topics include auditing agent performance and addressing social, economic, legal and environmental implications.
quote_evidence: argue that these tools do not qualify for authorship because they cannot be held morally responsible for their contributions
human scientists who use AIRAs have three key authorship responsibilities
We also reject the use of the term “scientist” to refer to these tools
why_it_matters_hint: Gives journals and labs an ethical framework as AI agents start doing research.
event_date: 2026 (publication date not stated in text read)
notes: Opinion/ethics paper, not an experiment; the authors' argument, not a rule.
